title: The Difference Between a Conversation and a Pitch
content:
###  **Homeowners Have Excellent Instincts** 

By the time someone has lived in a house for a few years, they have been pitched at their own front door dozens of times. They recognize the rhythm of it immediately — the opening line, the pause, the pivot toward the ask. 

The moment a homeowner identifies a pitch, the conversation is effectively over regardless of what is said next. 

###  **What a Conversation Sounds Like** 

A conversation starts with the house rather than the company. It asks before it tells. It allows for the possibility that the homeowner does not need anything at all — and it ends politely and quickly when that is the case. 

Counterintuitively, that willingness to end the interaction is a large part of what keeps people in it. 

###  **Why This Produces Better Outcomes** 

Homeowners who have a genuine conversation remember it. Some schedule something right away. Many do not, and reach out weeks later when the timing is right — which almost never happens after a pitch. 

### **Why It Is Harder to Do** 

Pitches are trainable. Conversations depend on the person. That is why the hiring standard matters more than the script, and why we spend more effort on who is at the door than on what they are told to say.
